props._notes:
2026-09-04, with the no-published-price decision. The site
               publishes no price, so the one thing this page has to say is
               that a date and a problem are enough to start with. Nothing
               else on this page changed.

2026-08-27, from the buyer-questions pass. Calls happen on
               request (Daniel's practice) but no number publishes — his call.
               One plain line, not a promise stack.

Static host, so this posts to formsubmit.co rather than a server
           action. _next is the confirmation page.
           No honeypot, on purpose: a hidden _honey field makes formsubmit
           drop the submission silently while still redirecting to /thanks/,
           and browser autofill fills hidden fields it can classify. That
           combination cost us a live corporate enquiry the week of
           2026-08-24 while blocking no observable spam — formsubmit's own
           server-side filtering is the spam layer. If spam volume ever
           becomes a problem, escalate to a relay that logs submissions,
           never back to a silent trap.

2026-09-23, Daniel: the form was eleven fields with four
             required, and the required one was labelled "Anything else".
             The site's own promise everywhere else is "send us the date and
             the venue", so that is what the form asks now. Three required
             fields, two optional, and the act field only appears when an
             Inquire link has already answered it. Company, phone, event
             type, guest count and "what needs covering" all go in the one
             box if the buyer wants to say them, and we ask the rest by
             reply.

Added with the roster restructure 2026-08-15. Every Inquire link
               on the site carries ?act=<id> and acts.js preselects it here, so
               an enquiry that started on an act page arrives naming the act
               rather than making the planner say it twice. Since 2026-09-23
               the field ships hidden and disabled, and acts.js shows it only
               when the link named an act, so nobody else scrolls a roster.
